For analyses of PISA achievement, analysts typically apply the PISA sampling weights and use the OECD/IEA-provided variance estimation approach (including replicate methods where available) to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals. Because this document is a country factsheet rather than an ML modeling paper, it does not specify whether weights/replicate weights were applied in the computations shown; users should follow the PISA 2022 technical documentation and database guidance for the correct weight and uncertainty estimation variables.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 country factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Colombia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably comparing 2018 vs 2022 and 2012 vs 2022). It reports mean performance comparisons with the OECD average and selected comparison countries, as well as proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2+ and Level 5/6) and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic gradients and gender differences. The assessment design uses two two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different test questions and subject combinations, plus a student background questionnaire (~35 minutes) and a school principal questionnaire. The factsheet also notes COVID-19-related disruptions and provides caution for countries/economies where sampling standards were not fully met; for Colombia, it states that all data met PISA quality standards. No predictive modeling or ML estimation is conducted in this note; it is descriptive and benchmark-oriented, with uncertainty communicated via confidence intervals.
